questions.question: A box 4 × 3 × 2 has its height doubled (now 4 × 3 × 4). Its volume changes from 24 to:

Why does surface area NOT simply double when only the height doubles?
options: Some faces contain the height and scale; the top and bottom do not, so the total scales by no clean factor
Surface area never changes under scaling
Because surface area always scales by k³
Because the net becomes a different shape

questions.question: After doubling only the height of the 4 × 3 × 2 box, the new surface area is:
A cylinder's radius is doubled, height unchanged. The volume multiplies by:
Why does k on the radius give k² on the cylinder's volume?
options: The radius is squared in V = πr² h, so it enters the product twice
It is a rounding effect of π

questions.question: Cylinder with V = 300π: triple the radius, keep the height. The new volume is:
Multiplying only the HEIGHT of a cylinder by k multiplies the volume by:
options: k, because h appears once in πr² h

subtopics.title: One Brick, Then a Wall of Doubles

questions.question: How many original bricks build a brick doubled in EVERY direction?
options: 8 — two along each of the three directions

questions.question: Making the brick twice as tall and nothing else multiplies its volume by:
options: 2 — a second identical layer on top

Because paint covers only half the faces
Because k is squared in every formula

questions.question: Grow every side by 10%. The extra paint needed is:

options: They grow at the same rate

options: Nothing — k below 1 is normal for enlargements
